what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: The work outgrew one site and split into nineteen
sections.para: On 11 August the thinking behind sgit was one website; by 26 August there were twenty repositories, nineteen of them siblings on *.sgit.ai, fifteen created in the last five days. Nobody planned it. It happened because the work outgrew its shape, and the split changed the writing.

sections.label: What forced it
sections.line: Arguments beyond sgit each needed their own version history
sections.para: A section promises it belongs to the thing it sits in, which stopped holding once the writing answered questions beyond sgit, such as accepting risk or maps as claims. Each argument needed room, its own readers and above all its own version history, since nineteen arguments in one changelog make an unreadable record.

sections.label: What it cost
sections.line: Splitting hurt discovery, consistency and cross-linking
sections.para: Nineteen domain names mean nothing to a new reader, so discovery got worse first. One stylesheet became a matter of discipline rather than construction. Links between sites became claims that can drift: an audit found graphs.sgit.ai pointing at sentinel.sgit.ai, which does not exist, instead of sg-sentinel.sgit.ai.

sections.label: What we did about discovery
sections.line: The directory now starts from the reader's question
sections.para: A list of nineteen cards had to be read before it helped, so the directory now opens with seventeen question-to-site lines, then five groups by area, then a table of all nineteen. That gives three ways in. Every thesis is quoted from the site's own H1 or lede, because summaries drift and quotations visibly fail.

sections.label: The thing that made it cheap
sections.line: A shared generator makes adding a site one file
sections.para: Every site uses the same generator, stylesheet, release script and validator, and publishing means adding one file. Adding a twentieth site to the index is one markdown file with a category and a one-line thesis. The same property lets two agents publish on the same day without conflict.

sections.label: Where it is honest
sections.line: Unbuilt sites say so plainly rather than being hidden
sections.para: skills.sgit.ai has a repository and DNS but nothing published, and is listed as not published yet rather than omitted. Most sites are arguments, not products: sg-sentinel says NOT BUILT, risks.sgit.ai has zero lines of code, and wardley-maps is PROPOSED. The house style publishes the argument first and states its worth.
